text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The United Nations rejects Algeria's invitation to send observers to supervise the June 5 parliamentary elections. The U.N will dispatch only a small technical team to support other observers from the Arab League and the Organisation of African Unity.
- Finance Minister Abdelkrim Harchaoui installs an insurance national council to prepare the sector for competition under free market rules.
- The government will open the water distribution business to private investors.
- The Socialist Forces Front to hold a leadership meeting on Thursday to announce the party's participation in the elections.
- University teachers to stage a three-day strike on April 12 over pay.
- The newly created National Democratic Party fails to draw enough supporters in the northeastern town of Tizi-Ouzou.
- Tahar Zbiri, a former army officer who attempted a coup against the government in 1967, was appointed deputy chief of an independent committee to oversee the forthcoming elections.
- Political sources say members of the outlawed Islamic Salvation Front want to compete in the elections under the banner of the secular Socialist Forces Front (FFS).
